question: Will any presidential candidate win outright in the first round of the Brazil election?
resolution_criteria:
Presidential elections are scheduled to be held in Brazil on October 4, 2026. A second round will be held if no candidate secures more than 50% of the valid votes in the first round.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any candidate wins this election in the first round. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the result of the first round of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

# Research report 1 of 2

I couldn't confirm any September 2026 poll. The latest poll data I could verify is from May 2026, and it shows Lula leading the first round well short of the 50% of valid votes needed to win outright. Many search results were dated after 2026-09-26, so I left them out as you asked.

## 1. Resolution source

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The main candidates are Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Others in the race include Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, Renan Santos and Augusto Cury, and at different points pollsters also tested Ciro Gomes and Ratinho Júnior. With that many candidates, every poll I found leaves the leader below 50% of valid votes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- I could not find any first-round poll from September 2026 published before 2026-09-26. Searches kept returning later material, which I excluded. The forecaster should check Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel for releases from 1 to 25 September.
- 2026-07/08: Wikipedia's polling table lists a Quaest poll from late July to early August with the top two at 39 and 30, probably Lula 39%, Flávio 30%. The column labels were unclear, so this needs checking. [Wikipedia polling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Brazilian_presidential_election)
- 2026-05-05: Real Big Data, scenario without Ciro: Lula 48%, Flávio 34%, Caiado 5%, Zema 4%, measured as total votes. [Bem Paraná](https://www.bemparana.com.br/noticias/politica/lula-e-flavio-bolsonaro-empatam-em-1o-e-2o-turnos-aponta/), [Jovem Pan](https://jovempan.com.br/noticias/politica/realtime-bigdata-lula-empata-com-flavio-caiado-e-ciro-em-eventual-2o-turno.html)
- 2026-05: Futura/Apex: Lula 42.7%, Flávio 35.6% in the first round. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/futura-apex-lula-tem-427-e-flavio-356-no-1o-turno/)
- 2026-04: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg: Lula 46.6%, Flávio 39.7%, Caiado 3.3%. [Portal de Prefeitura](https://portaldeprefeitura.com.br/eleicoes/lula-lidera-primeiro-turno-empata-flavio-zema-atlas/620180/)
- 2026-03: Datafolha: Lula led every first-round scenario, and in a runoff Lula had 46% to Flávio's 43%. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)
- 2026-01: Genial/Quaest: Lula 35%, Flávio 26%, Ratinho Jr. 9%. [Quaest via tagteam](https://tagteam.harvard.edu/hub_feeds/3884/feed_items/17183858/content)
- Across these polls, Lula leads the first round by about 7 to 14 points but stays in the 35-48% range of total votes. Runoff simulations are mostly technical ties, which suggests a closely split electorate.

## 4. Base rates
- Since 1989, Brazil has held 9 direct presidential elections. Two were won in the first round: Fernando Henrique Cardoso in 1994 and 1998. The other seven went to a runoff: 1989, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022. The last first-round win was 28 years ago.
- 2022: Lula took 48.4% of valid votes to Bolsonaro's 43.2%, and the race went to a runoff even though Lula slightly beat his poll numbers. The polls underestimated Bolsonaro. [Inquirer/AFP](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1674150/brazil-election-goes-to-runoff-as-bolsonaro-beats-polls/amp)
- 2006: Lula got 48.6% and was forced into a runoff, even though some final polls showed him close to an outright win.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has this exact market ("Will any presidential candidate win outright in the first round of the Brazil election?"). An aggregator snapshot showed "Yes" at about 13¢. I could not confirm the date of that snapshot, so it may not reflect the price on 2026-09-26. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x087469b4129c64c688397028059dfd366796adbd426e0079ee4cfdd2e4a07b61)
- Kalshi has a matching market, KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04. I could not get its current price. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04)
- There is also a related Polymarket market on the first-round margin of victory. [Lines.com](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-margin-of-victory)
- I found no expert or model forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The final TV debates take place in the last week of the campaign.
- Late tactical voting ("voto útil") could squeeze the smaller candidates, which would make an outright win more likely. An outright win would need the leader at roughly 50%+ of valid votes, about 3-5 points above the best recent poll numbers I could verify.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I'm writing up the brief now. I'm leaving out everything I found that was published after the 2026-09-26 cutoff.

## 1. Resolution source
- Rule (Brazilian Constitution, Art. 77): a candidate wins in the first round only with more than 50% of **valid** votes. Blank and spoiled (null) ballots are not counted as valid votes.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. In the polls I could date before the cutoff, no candidate is close to 50% of valid votes. The front-runners, Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), are in the mid-30s or lower in total votes, and several minor candidates split the rest.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-07: Genial/Quaest poll (fieldwork Sept 4-7, 2,004 interviews, margin of error ±2 pts), first round in total votes: Lula 36%, Flávio Bolsonaro 29%, Augusto Cury 8%, Renan Santos (Missão) 3%, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) 3%, Romeu Zema (Novo) 2%. Excluding undecided, blank and null answers, Lula would be roughly in the mid-40s of valid votes, below 50%. That share is my own rough calculation, not a figure Quaest published. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/quaest-no-1o-turno-lula-tem-36-flavio-29-e-cury-8/)
- 2026-03 (Reuters/Datafolha): Lula 46% vs Flávio 43% in a runoff simulation, a technical tie. Lula led every first-round scenario but well below a majority. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)
- 2026-01 (Quaest): Lula 35%, Flávio 26% in the first round. [Harvard TagTeam/Quaest](https://tagteam.harvard.edu/hub_feeds/3884/feed_items/17183858/content)
- I could not find a Datafolha, AtlasIntel or Quaest poll dated between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-26.

## 4. Base rates
- Brazilian presidential elections since 1989 under the two-round system: an outright first-round win happened twice in 9 elections, both by Fernando Henrique Cardoso (1994 with about 54%, 1998 with about 53%).
- Every election since then went to a runoff: 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022, so 0 of the last 6.
- 2022 is the closest recent case. Lula got 48.4% of valid votes in the first round, short of 50%, even though some final polls had shown him near or above 50% of valid votes. Polls underestimated Bolsonaro by several points. [CBC](https://amp.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.6603351)
- In 2026, the clearest polling difference from 2022 is that both front-runners are well below 50% of valid votes, with Augusto Cury and others taking a meaningful share.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has a market with this exact title. Snapshots I found from earlier in 2026 priced "Yes" at about 10-13%. I could not get a timestamped price close to 2026-09-26 because the aggregator page would not load. [SimpleFunctions mirror](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x087469b4129c64c688397028059dfd366796adbd426e0079ee4cfdd2e4a07b61)
- Kalshi has a related market, KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04 ("Will anyone win outright in the first round..."). I could not find a current price. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04), [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/odds/will-anyone-win-outright-in-the-brazil-presidential-election/6965)
- I found no formal expert or model forecast of a first-round win.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The last week of the campaign (Sept 26 to Oct 3): final TV debates, and final Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls, usually published the day before the vote. Watch for any candidate getting close to 50% of valid votes.
- Tactical voting: supporters of minor candidates (Cury, Caiado, Zema, Santos) switching to a front-runner at the last minute could push that front-runner up. Their combined share in early September was about 16%.

Sources: [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/quaest-no-1o-turno-lula-tem-36-flavio-29-e-cury-8/), [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html), [Harvard TagTeam](https://tagteam.harvard.edu/hub_feeds/3884/feed_items/17183858/content), [CBC](https://amp.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.6603351), [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x087469b4129c64c688397028059dfd366796adbd426e0079ee4cfdd2e4a07b61), [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/odds/will-anyone-win-outright-in-the-brazil-presidential-election/6965)

forecasts.reasoning:
- For Yes:
  - Lula polled 46.6% (AtlasIntel, April 2026) and 48% total in one scenario (Real Big Data, May 2026).
  - Late tactical voting could squeeze minor candidates, who held about 16% combined in early September.
  - Polymarket priced Yes at about 10-13% earlier in 2026.
- For No:
  - Quaest (Sept 7, 2026) shows Lula at only 36% of total votes, down from spring levels.
  - Flávio holds a solid 29-30%, and Cury takes 8%.
  - In 2022, Lula got 48.4% of valid votes after polls had shown him near 50%, and polls underestimated the right.
  - Runoff simulations are technical ties, which points to a polarized electorate.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- No: Lula finishes around 44-47% of valid votes, Flávio around 36-40%, minor candidates keep around 10-15%, and the race goes to a runoff on October 25. This is the most likely path.
- Yes: Cury's and the centrists' support collapses into a late anti-polarization swing toward Lula, Flávio stagnates, and Lula outperforms his final polls by 5 or more points, reaching 50.5%.

(f) **From base rate to final probability.** The raw historical rate is 22%, but conditioning on the current polling gap of 6-8 points short of 50% of valid votes brings it down to the low single digits. The earlier 10-13% market prices came from the spring, when Lula polled higher, and the September data is weaker for him. I allow some room for polling error, tactical consolidation, and the chance I missed late-September polls. My estimate is about 6%.

Probability: 6%

(e) Scenarios:

(f) Reasoning: I start from the roughly 22% historical rate, or about 12% from the earlier market price. I then adjust downward because the most recent dated poll puts Lula about 6 points below the threshold one month out. Closing that gap would take an unusually large late swing combined with a polling error running against the historical pattern. The final week leaves some room for tactical voting and polling error, so I keep a modest tail.

Probability: 5%

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** Lula finishes around 44-47% of valid votes, Flávio around 38-42%, the minor candidates keep 10% or more, and the race goes to a runoff on October 25.
- **Yes:** Cury and the center-right candidates collapse in the final week, anti-Bolsonaro tactical voting flows to Lula, and he reaches 50.5%.

**(f) Devil's advocate and final adjustment.** I lean strongly No. The best case for Yes is the following:
- Valid-vote math is more generous than headline numbers suggest. With 16% undecided, blank or null, 36% of total votes becomes about 43% of valid votes. Undecided voters could break disproportionately toward the incumbent.
- Brazilian polls have errors of 3-5 points.
- Some pollsters, such as AtlasIntel and Real Big Data, showed Lula higher in the spring.
- The 10-13% market price shows other traders see real tail risk.

A path where Lula finds 6-7 points in a week is not impossible.

But the trend runs the wrong way for Yes. Lula's share fell from the mid-40s in some spring polls to 36% in September. Cury's 8% looks like a genuine anti-polarization vote, not soft support that will migrate to Lula. A late surge for the second-placed candidate would also help produce a runoff, not prevent one. The market snapshot was not timestamped and likely predates the September data, so I discount it.

I move down from the roughly 22% raw base rate and the earlier market price of about 12%. My final estimate is about 4%.

Probability: 4%
